questions.prompt: What is a pipeable operator, at its core?

options.text: A function that takes a source Observable and returns a new Observable
A subclass of Observable
A value emitted by a Subject
A method on the Observable prototype

questions.explanation: Its type is OperatorFunction<T, R>: (source: Observable<T>) => Observable<R>. Anything with that shape works inside .pipe().

questions.prompt: What is the simplest, preferred way to build a custom operator?

options.text: Compose existing operators with the standalone pipe() function
Extend the Observable class
Patch a method onto Observable.prototype
Always use the Observable constructor manually

questions.explanation: Most custom operators are just pipe(op1, op2, ...) wrapped in a function. Composition handles teardown and the Observable contract for you.

questions.prompt: When writing a low-level operator with `new Observable`, what must you do? Select all that apply.

options.text: Forward next values to the output subscriber
Forward error and complete notifications
Return a teardown that unsubscribes from the source
Avoid subscribing to the source at all

questions.explanation: You subscribe to the source and forward all three notification types, and you return teardown so the source subscription is released. Not subscribing would mean no values flow.

questions.prompt: Type the RxJS type used to annotate an operator whose input and output types are the SAME (T to T): `______________________<T>`.
questions.explanation: MonoTypeOperatorFunction<T> is the special case of OperatorFunction<T, T> where the type is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Why is composition (pipe) preferred over the Observable constructor for custom operators?

options.text: It is simpler and automatically forwards notifications and handles teardown
The Observable constructor is deprecated
pipe operators run faster in every case
The constructor cannot emit more than one value

questions.explanation: Composing existing operators means less code and fewer chances to break the contract — teardown and notification forwarding are handled for you. Reserve the constructor for genuinely custom subscription logic.

questions.prompt: How do you make a custom operator configurable, like `debounceTime(300)`?

options.text: Write a function that takes parameters and returns the OperatorFunction
Set a global config variable before piping
Pass the parameter to subscribe()
Custom operators cannot take parameters

questions.explanation: A configurable operator is a factory: `const op = (arg) => pipe(...)` returning an OperatorFunction, so call sites read like built-ins, e.g. source$.pipe(op(300)).
